extracted.intended_audience: empirical researchers, economists, and policy analysts studying patent filing behavior and standard-essential patents (SEPs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological standards for constructing samples and estimating effects of standards/SEPs on continuation and child filing behavior using application-quarter level hazard/OLS models. Includes definitions of SEPs/controls, covariates, fixed effects, estimation choices, and placebo/DID specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of observation and sample inclusion (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit of observation is an application-quarter. An application is included in the sample from its filing quarter to the earliest of the filing quarter of its first continuation, the latest disposal quarter of an application in its U.S. patent family or the end of year 2016 if its family is still pending (i.e. at least one filing in the U.S. patent family is still under examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes clarify that the sample period/end rule can vary by table: some specifications instead include an application until the earliest of its first-continuation filing quarter, the quarter of disposal, or the end of 2016 if still pending. The unit being application-quarter implies longitudinal observation until one of these censoring events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of SEP (primary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A SEP is the earliest U.S. utility patent application of a domestic patent family that contains at least one U.S. utility patent application declared essential for a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the paper's primary operationalization of a standard-essential patent application (SEP) used in treatment indicators. Alternative/declared SEP definitions appear in other tables (see 'declared SEPs' entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of control application
rubrics_metrics.description: A control application is the earliest U.S. utility patent application of a domestic patent family that does not contain any U.S. utility patent applications declared essential for a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls are chosen to be the earliest family application lacking any declared-essential applications; controls are placed into the same art-unit-examiner-filing-quarter groups as SEPs when forming the comparison sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping requirement for sample (art-unit-examiner-filing-quarter groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample contains SEPs and control applications in art-unit-examiner-filing-quarter groups with at least one SEP and one control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several specifications restrict the sample to examiner-art-unit-filing-quarter groups that include both treated (SEP) and control applications to enable within-group comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables for application characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Control variables for the characteristics of the earliest U.S. utility patent application of a family include indicators for applications that claim priority to provisional applications, PCT applications or foreign applications, an indicator for applications filed by small entities, and the natural logarithms of the number of independent claims, the number of words per independent claim, and the number of inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These controls capture observable application complexity, scope, and applicant size and are included in most specifications to adjust for covariate differences between SEPs and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed effects and higher-order age controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications include Quarter FE, Age FE, AU-E-FQ FE, and polynomial age controls (Age2, age3 & age4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed effects and polynomial age terms are used to soak up time, age, and examiner/art-unit filing-quarter group heterogeneity. AU-E-FQ denotes art-unit–examiner–filing-quarter fixed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation methods and model types
rubrics_metrics.description: Models reported include OLS pooled cross-section specifications and variants described as 'Myopic tech & cohort controls' and 'Quasi-myopic tech & cohort controls'; tables label columns by model number and type (e.g., pooled cross-section (1), (4); myopic (2),(3); quasi-myopic (5),(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice among pooled OLS vs. myopic/quasi-myopic specifications reflects different controls for anticipatory/temporal effects; researchers should report which specification is used and interpret coefficients accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction variables used to measure standard effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Key explanatory variables include interactions such as PostStandard × SEP and lagged interactions Standard (t − k) × SEP (for k = 1..4) to estimate the effect of standard publication timing on outcome rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reported coefficients on PostStandard × SEP and the lagged Standard × SEP terms capture contemporaneous and dynamic effects of standard publication on continuation/child filing; models show multiple lags to trace dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing control-variable values and sample restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Models (3) and (6) are estimated after dropping applications with missing values for the control variables and keeping only examiner-art-unit-filing-quarter groups with at least one SEP and one control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit robustness/sample restriction: dropping missing covariate observations and enforcing within-group treated/control presence can change sample size and estimates; authors report which models apply this restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard errors and significance notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard errors are clustered by application in parentheses. Significance notation: *** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clustering by application accounts for within-application serial correlation across quarters. Report both clustered SEs and conventional significance markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declared SEP sample (alternative SEP operationalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: For declared SEPs, the sample contains SEPs that are mentioned in patent disclosure letters and are filed before the quarter of publication of the earliest standard linked to the application, and control applications in art-unit-examiner-filing-quarter groups with at least one SEP and one control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrower 'declared SEP' definition uses disclosed-essentiality evidence (patent disclosure letters) and imposes timing (filed before publication of linked standard) to avoid post-treatment composition. Applicable notes clarify slight differences in censoring (e.g., earliest of first continuation filing quarter, quarter of disposal, or end of 2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome variables and sample censoring for different outcomes (continuation, child, declared continuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuation-filing outcomes the unit remains application-quarter; inclusion rules sometimes state an application is observed until the earliest of filing quarter of first continuation, the quarter of disposal, or end of 2016 if still pending. For child filing outcomes analogous inclusion/censoring rules and SEP definitions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers must state which censoring rule they use for each outcome table; notes in tables A8–A10 and related panels specify the exact censoring rule used in that table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference-in-differences estimators and placebo tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference-in-differences specifications are reported (DIDM, DIDl) that estimate PostStandard × SEP effects across multiple post-periods (Effect0..Effect4) and report PreStandard × SEP placebo estimates (Placebo−1..Placebo−4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DID specifications include random/ matched sampling variants (e.g., 'SEPs and Controls picked randomly' vs 'matched on Pre-standard CONs') and test for pre-trends via placebo lead coefficients. Researchers should present both effect estimates and placebo/null-pretrend tests.
